card.name: Concomitant and similarity wording in interactions
card.fires_on: The end of "concomitant" (the "itant" piece) in drug interaction sections, and linking words like "that" or "similar" in sentences about combining or comparing drugs.

modes.label: Concomitant use
modes.description: The closing piece of "concomitant" before "administration" or "use" of two drugs.
modes.example: The concom<<itant>> administration of SIMBRINZA and oral

modes.label: Linking word after recommendation
modes.description: "that" after "it is recommended" in interaction advice.
modes.example: it is recommended<< that>> mycophenolic acid delayed-release

modes.label: Similarity or overlap words
modes.description: Words like "similar" or "overlapping" comparing drug effects or binding.
modes.example: human plasma proteins is<< similar>> to the individual components.

card.writes: It seems to promote word endings and code-like pieces while suppressing "similar" and "comparable" words, so it steers away from repeating a similarity word.
card.plain: It lights up on "concomitant" and nearby wording when a label discusses using two drugs together or comparing them.
